approved: Parliamentary Joint Committee on the Australia Fund Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would create a parliamentary committee to study setting up an Australia Fund.
The committee would hold hearings across Australia and review bankruptcy and insolvency laws.
The fund would be able to provide emergency relief, loans, loan guarantees, and other financial support to rural and manufacturing businesses during crises.
Establishes a Joint Parliamentary Committee to investigate an Australia Fund.
The committee would examine the impact of natural disasters and market fluctuations on rural Australia.
The committee would review bankruptcy and insolvency laws to help companies trade through difficulties.
The committee would consider introducing United States Chapter 11-style provisions.
The committee would report its findings and recommendations to Parliament.
Rural and manufacturing industries, businesses, and communities affected by natural disasters or financial crises.

Argued in support of the Parliamentary Joint Committee on the Australia Fund Bill, which would establish a committee to inquire into whether a rural and manufacturing industries fund is needed to respond to droughts, floods and other crises, noting the proposal originated with the member for Fairfax and the Palmer United Party.

Argued that the Parliamentary Joint Committee on the Australia Fund Bill is a delaying tactic by a government that has cut almost half a billion dollars of manufacturing and industry funding, saying the committee process would not deliver help to struggling farmers and industries until after the next election.
